topic: Diagnosing @Transactional self-invocation in Spring proxy mode
tomorrowTopic: Testing Spring transaction boundaries with Testcontainers

hook.headline: The annotation is there. The transaction is not.
hook.hook: A Spring method can carry @Transactional yet skip its transaction advice when another method on the same instance calls it directly.
hook.visualCaption: In Spring's default proxy mode, transaction advice runs when a call crosses the transactional proxy.
hook.microExample: external call → proxy → advice; self-call → target method directly

mentalModel.title: Follow the method call
mentalModel.coreIdea: Spring's default declarative transaction mode uses an AOP proxy. Calls entering through that proxy can trigger TransactionInterceptor; a method calling another method on the same target instance does not re-enter the proxy, so the inner annotation is not independently applied.
mentalModel.keyOutcome: An annotation changes behaviour only when the configured transaction infrastructure actually intercepts the invocation.

code.title: REQUIRES_NEW that never starts
code.intro: This internal call does not cross the Spring proxy in the default proxy-based transaction mode.
code.highlightReason: The self-call invokes the target directly, so proxy-based transaction advice does not create the requested REQUIRES_NEW boundary here.
code.takeaway: Move the transactional operation behind another Spring bean when you need a proxy-intercepted boundary.
code.professionalNote: AspectJ transaction mode uses weaving rather than proxy interception, so the self-invocation limitation described here does not apply in the same way.

production.title: Why did the audit row roll back?
production.scenario: An order transaction calls AuditService.record(), expecting recordInNewTx() to commit independently. The order later fails, and the audit row disappears with the outer transaction.
problems: The internal call bypasses the proxy, so REQUIRES_NEW is not applied at that method boundary.
An existing outer transaction can make the code appear transactional while hiding the missing independent boundary.
production.professionalApproach: Trace the runtime call path, not just annotations. Put the REQUIRES_NEW operation on a separate proxied bean, then verify independent commit and rollback behaviour with an integration test.
production.debugClue: A rollback test shows the supposedly independent audit insert disappearing whenever the outer order transaction rolls back.

interview.question: A public method annotated REQUIRES_NEW is called from another method in the same Spring bean, but no new transaction appears. Why?
interview.answer: With Spring's default proxy-based transaction management, transaction advice runs when the invocation crosses the proxy. A self-call stays on the target object, so the REQUIRES_NEW method is not intercepted and does not create that new boundary. I would move it to another Spring bean or deliberately choose another transaction mechanism, then verify the behaviour with an integration test.
